claim: A one-hour online module (CHAMPS KNOW; base rates, comparison classes, updating, calibration) improved human forecasters' Brier score by 6-12% over randomized controls in each of four tournament years.
agent_test: Not testable as a module; test the content as fixed scaffold steps. Same questions, equal tokens: scaffold with steps vs plain.

claim: The four yearly cohorts in Chang et al. are one research programme, not four independent replications. No independent replication of the one-hour probability module was found; the nearest outside tests (Kelly & Mandel 2024, 70 analysts, pre/post, different course; Stone et al. 2023, lab feedback) test other calibration training and show confidence shifts, not a replication.
agent_test: Read Sedlmeier & Gigerenzer 2001 and Karimi Motahhar & Gruca 2025 (located, blocked).

claim: The training effect shrank from 12% (Y2) to 6-7% (Y3-Y4) even as the module grew richer; participants were self-selected volunteers making 30+ forecasts per year.
agent_test: Check whether a scaffold gain also shrinks as the base model gets stronger.

claim: Of the trained principles, only citing comparison classes (reference class / outside view) went with better forecasts (standardized Brier 0.17 vs control 0.49); the other cited principles were not better or were worse. This is correlational (self-classified explanations).
agent_test: Ablate: scaffold with only the reference-class step vs the full list at equal tokens.

claim: Training raised forecasts per question (Y3 4.27 vs 1.90; Y1 1.58 vs 1.35) but the mediation of the training effect by forecasts per question is significant only in Y1 (p=.01) and Y3 (p=.05) per the Results text; Y2 and Y4 are not significant. The paper's own summary says three of four years, which the Results text does not support.
agent_test: Compare agent with forced update rounds vs a single pass at equal tokens.

claim: Training halved overconfidence in a large multi-year set (4.3% to 2.0% alone; 2.8% to 0.7% in teams) while hit rate rose only about 0.8 points; most of the gain is lower confidence.
agent_test: Measure ECE and Brier with and without a calibration step at equal tokens; check whether only confidence shifted.

claim: Earlier lab calibration training (Lichtenstein & Fischhoff 1980: 45 minutes plus 22 one-hour sessions; Stone & Opel 2000: 6 two-hour sessions) is described by Moore et al. (opened) as degrading over time and transferring poorly. The original papers still were not opened; exact numbers are missing. A 2024 pre/post study of analysts found no cross-task transfer (r=-.06 miscalibration, -.10 bias).
agent_test: Motivates testing transfer of an agent's calibration step across question types.

claim: Telling people about biases (didactic) is weak; process-based techniques such as reference classes and asking twice work better.
agent_test: Compare an awareness prompt vs a procedural reference-class step.

claim: Prompting LLMs with human-style forecasting training steps barely helps: the best prompts (frequency-based, base-rate-first, step-back) lowered Brier only 0.011 to 0.014 in mixed models (adj p=.774) and 0.015 to 0.019 in one-sample t-tests (adj p .022-.036).
agent_test: Run the reference-class step alone vs a token-matched filler step, several runs per item, on the target model.

claim: Bayesian-reasoning and Propose-Evaluate-Select prompts made LLM forecasts significantly worse (mixed model +0.030 and +0.033; t-tests +0.025 and +0.028 Brier) and moved forecasts furthest from 50% (distance 0.199 and 0.175 vs control 0.134). No shrink or calibration post-step was tested by anyone found.
schema_part: Section 4b (do not add an explicit Bayes step)
agent_test: Track distance from 50% and Brier in our scaffold.

claim: In Study 2 with newer models (o1, o1-mini) no prompt helped and a superforecaster-authored prompt was significantly worse (+0.023). Prompt gains do not generalize.
agent_test: Run the same prompts on the model we actually use.

claim: Reasoning-prompt content alone adds little for LLM forecasting; retrieval (about 0.020 Brier) and fine-tuning (0.007) carry the gain in Halawi et al. (no retrieval, no fine-tune 0.206 vs 0.208 plain baseline; full system 0.179), even though their scratchpad already had a base-rate and calibration-check step. A base-rate pipeline also lost to a one-line prompt in Pratt et al. (0.1562 vs 0.1221).
agent_test: Ablate retrieval vs reasoning steps in the agent.

claim: Outcome-based RL on a Brier reward improved a 14B model from 0.215 to 0.190-0.192 and cut ECE from 0.089 to 0.054-0.062, but stayed worse than the market (0.151); a randomized-label control moved Phi-4 only 0.221 to 0.214.
agent_test: Use as a ceiling reference, not a method.

claim: Reward design matters in forecast training: accuracy-only reward gave worse-than-constant scores, and Brier-only produced Unknown answers in about 40% of samples.
agent_test: Watch for abstention collapse if we add a calibration reward.

claim: Top LLMs approach but do not reach superforecasters: ForecastBench 0.122 (best LLM) vs 0.121 public vs 0.096 superforecasters; o3 reached 0.135 on another question set. Brier is not comparable across sets, and the best LLMs partly used crowd freeze values.
agent_test: Always compare to controls on the same questions.

claim: Giving LLMs the human crowd median improved GPT-4 and Claude 2 accuracy 17-28%; LLM assistants raised human accuracy 24-28%; an LLM crowd matched a human crowd (0.20 vs 0.19).
agent_test: Equal-token test: N samples averaged vs one long chain.

claim: Ensembling helps a tool-using forecasting agent (0.169 vs 0.180 single) but not base GPT-4o (0.218 vs 0.210).
agent_test: Test ensembling only after the scaffold; do not assume it helps.

claim: Feedback training did not help experts forecasting cancer-trial outcomes (Brier 0.22 vs 0.21, p=.51) though the pooled crowd did well (0.17); a short briefing widened intervals but hit rates stayed below 80%.
agent_test: Boundary case: training gain depends on domain and feedback quality.

claim: LLM forecast evaluation is easily contaminated: date-filtered retrieval leaks, pastcasting runs vary from under 20% to over 80%, and forecasts are inconsistent across related questions.
agent_test: Use frozen retrieval and repeat each item several times.

claim: At least a year of persistence is supported in part. Chang Table 9 shows trained veterans (same people, kept in condition) beating control veterans in Y2 (0.34 vs 0.39, n=153/148) and Y3 (0.33 vs 0.36, n=53/56), and Moore finds the overconfidence cut stable across the forecasting year. Confounds: attrition selection, a revised module in later years, and continuous Brier feedback. There was no delayed retest without feedback.
agent_test: Re-open Chang for any within-person follow-up.

claim: The mediation by forecasts per question is non-significant in Y2 and Y4 of Chang et al. (Y1 p=.01, Y3 p=.05), settling the Y2-versus-Y4 dispute: both fail.
agent_test: Do not rely on forced update rounds as the explained mechanism.

claim: Calibration training can shift bias rather than improve skill: in 70 analysts, interval-task bias fell (d=1.17) but binary-task bias rose toward underconfidence (d=0.37), with uncorrelated changes across tasks.
agent_test: Test a shrink step for over-shrinking on easy items.

claim: Across 38 prompts and four LLMs, an explicit anti-overconfidence instruction had no effect (0.000 mixed, -0.004 t-test), and the closest match to the human comparison-class step (Multiple Reference Classes) gave -0.004 mixed (adj p .774) and -0.009 t-test (adj p .233). The apparently helpful base-rate prompts reach significance only in uncorrected-structure t-tests.
agent_test: No token-matched test exists; run one.

claim: Prompt-induced shifts in the overall probability level can create or hide a Brier effect: a rationale-first prompt raised probabilities and lost to a one-line prompt because most events resolved No (Pratt 2024), while Bayesian prompts increased distance from 50% (Schoenegger 2025).
agent_test: Always compare against a constant-base-rate forecast and a reversed-question test.

claim: Fine-tuning on Bayesian-assistant demonstrations (with its early uncertain guesses) beats fine-tuning on correct answers and generalizes across domains, while prompting alone did not help (Qiu 2025). No study tests worked examples versus abstract instructions for forecasting.
agent_test: Compare a few-shot trace of staged uncertain updates against an abstract rule at equal tokens.
